plugin.name: approval
plugin.config: name: approval enabled: true description: "Human-in-the-loop tool approval" config: timeout: 60.0 ask_list: []

plugin.name: compaction
plugin.config: name: compaction hooks: - round_end - tool_output enabled: true config: threshold: 0.75 window_size: 131072 # fallback — overridden by ModelConfig.context_window keep_count: 8 truncation: l1_threshold: 0.50 l2_threshold: 0.70 preview_chars: 100 window_ratio: 0.15 # safeguard threshold = window * ratio / avg_tools_per_round

tool.name: compact
tool.definition: name: compact description: Manually trigger context compaction. Summarizes old messages and inserts a compact boundary marker, keeping recent messages intact. Use when the conversation is getting long and you want to free context space. parameters: type: object properties: {} annotations: readOnlyHint: false idempotentHint: false destructiveHint: true

skills.skill:
name: compact description: Manual context compaction trigger prompt: | # Context Compaction
When the conversation history gets long, use `compact` to summarize old messages and free context window space. After compaction, the conversation continues with a summary of earlier context.
Compaction is also triggered automatically when token usage exceeds the threshold. Prefer manual compaction before reaching the automatic trigger point for a smoother experience. tools: - compact activation: kernel

plugin.name: error_handler
plugin.config: name: error_handler enabled: true description: "5-action recovery: abort, fallback, retry, skip, rollback" config: max_continuation: 3 max_compaction: 2 max_transport_retry: 3 backoff_base: 1.0 backoff_max: 30.0

plugin.name: eval
plugin.config:
name: eval hooks: [] # offline, not hook-mounted enabled: true config: trace_dir: ./data/traces eval_dir: ./eval judge: system_prompt: > You are an expert evaluator for AI agent behavior. Your role is to compare an agent's actual output against a reference (golden) standard. You are impartial, precise, and consistent. Ground every judgment in the specific content provided — never speculate about missing information, and clearly state when a comparison cannot be reliably made. Every evaluation must be reproducible: another evaluator reading your reasoning should arrive at the same conclusion. Always respond with valid JSON only, no markdown fences or extra text. prompts: tool_call_result_llm: | You are comparing the output of a tool call against the expected reference output.
User's original request: {user_input}
Tool: {tool_name} Expected output: <<<EXPECTED>>> {expected} <<<END>>>
Actual output: <<<ACTUAL>>> {actual} <<<END>>>
Determine whether the actual output is **semantically equivalent** to the expected output. Semantic equivalence means: both outputs convey the same functional information — they would lead the agent to the same next decision or action, even if wording, formatting, or verbosity differ.
Judgment criteria: - true : Core information is preserved. Minor formatting differences, extra details that do not change meaning, or different phrasing of the same facts are all acceptable. - false: Critical information is missing, contradictory facts are present, or the actual output is an error/failure while the expected was successful.
Edge cases: - If either output appears truncated, judge based on the available content. - If the actual output is an error/failure but the expected was successful, this is unequivocally false. - If both are errors/failures of the same type, they are equivalent (true). - Numeric values: treat ±5% deviation as equivalent unless precision is clearly critical to the user's request. - If the actual output contains the expected output verbatim plus extra surrounding context, it is still equivalent.
Respond with ONLY a JSON object (no markdown fences, no extra text): {{"match": <bool>, "reason": "<2-3 sentences explaining the key similarities or differences that determined your judgment>"}} output_quality: | You are evaluating the quality of an AI agent's final answer against a golden reference answer.
User's original request: {user_input}
Golden reference answer: <<<GOLDEN>>> {golden} <<<END>>>
Actual answer: <<<ACTUAL>>> {actual} <<<END>>>
Rate the actual answer on a 1–5 scale. The goal is NOT verbatim matching — a differently worded answer that serves the user equally well should score high. Conversely, a verbatim copy that misses the user's intent should score low.
Scoring rubric (anchor on the behavioral description, not the label): 5 — Excellent: Effectively addresses the user's request. Factually correct, complete, clear, and well-structured. A user would be fully satisfied. 4 — Good: Addresses the request but has minor flaws — slightly incomplete, mildly verbose, or missing a secondary detail. Still clearly useful. 3 — Adequate: Partially addresses the request. Contains some correct information but has notable omissions, unclear phrasing, or minor factual issues. A user would need to ask follow-up questions. 2 — Poor: Mostly incorrect, irrelevant, or so incomplete that the core request is not meaningfully answered. A user would reject this answer. 1 — Wrong/Harmful: Completely incorrect, contradicts the golden answer on key facts, or provides dangerously misleading information.
Important distinctions: - Factual errors are worse than stylistic issues (verbose but correct should not drop below 4). - An answer that is correct but less detailed than the golden answer may still score 4 if the essentials are there. - An answer that adds genuinely useful context beyond the golden answer should NOT be penalized — it can still score 5. - If both answers are functionally identical but phrased differently, score 5.
Respond with ONLY a JSON object (no markdown fences, no extra text): {{"score": <int 1-5>, "reason": "<2-3 sentences justifying the score with specific reference to what the actual answer did well or poorly>"}} trajectory_similarity: | You are evaluating whether an AI agent followed a correct procedure to fulfill the user's request.
User's original request: {user_input}
Golden trajectory (reference procedure): <<<GOLDEN>>> {golden} <<<END>>>
Actual trajectory (what the agent did): <<<ACTUAL>>> {actual} <<<END>>>
The golden trajectory is ONE correct way to solve the problem, not the ONLY correct way. The agent may take a different but equally valid path.
Trajectory format: each entry represents a turn with [turn N] prefixes. Entries show tool calls (call <name>), tool results (result: ok/fail), and model outputs (output: <text>).
Rate the actual trajectory on a 1–5 scale: 5 — Excellent match: Uses the same key tools/steps in a logical order to achieve the goal. Minor variations (extra benign calls, slightly different order for independent steps) are acceptable. 4 — Good match: Core approach is correct. Differs in some tool choices or order, but still reaches the goal competently. 3 — Partial match: Some correct steps but missing critical tool calls, wrong order for dependent steps, or includes clearly unnecessary detours. 2 — Poor match: The approach is largely wrong. Key tools are missing or misused. The agent seems to be guessing or going in circles. 1 — No match: Completely wrong approach, irrelevant tool calls, or the trajectory fails to address the user's request at all.
Weighting guidelines: - Using the right tools matters more than using them in the exact same order (unless the order reflects a hard dependency). - Extra benign tool calls that don't affect the outcome should not significantly lower the score. - Missing a critical tool that is essential to the solution should drop the score by at least 2 points. - If the actual trajectory achieves the same result through a genuinely different but equally sound approach, score 5.
Respond with ONLY a JSON object (no markdown fences, no extra text): {{"score": <int 1-5>, "reason": "<2-3 sentences justifying the score with specific reference to which steps matched or diverged>"}} output_quality_free: | You are evaluating the quality of an AI agent's final answer. You do NOT have a golden reference — evaluate the answer on its own merits.
Agent system prompt: {system_prompt} Available tools and descriptions: {tools}
User's original request: {user_input}
Agent's final answer: <<<ANSWER>>> {actual} <<<END>>>
Rate the answer on a 1–5 scale. The answer should be judged against what a reasonable agent with these instructions and tools SHOULD produce.
Scoring rubric: 5 — Excellent: Fully addresses the user's request. Correct, complete, well-structured, and aligned with the system prompt's constraints. If the system prompt limits behavior (e.g., brevity), compliance with that constraint IS quality. 4 — Good: Addresses the core request but has minor flaws — slightly incomplete, mildly verbose, or missing a secondary detail. 3 — Adequate: Partially addresses the request. Notable omissions or unclear phrasing. A user would need follow-up questions. 2 — Poor: Mostly does not address the request. Key information missing or wrong. A user would reject this answer. 1 — Wrong/Harmful: Completely irrelevant, contradicts the user's request, or violates explicit system prompt prohibitions.
Critical rules: - If the system prompt explicitly restricts behavior (format, length, content), compliance with those restrictions is REQUIRED for a high score. A brief answer that follows instructions is NOT a flaw — the constraint IS the expected behavior. - If system prompt or tools fields are empty, you are missing key context — note this in your reason and judge conservatively.
Respond with ONLY a JSON object (no markdown fences, no extra text): {{"score": <int 1-5>, "reason": "<2-3 sentences>"}} trajectory_similarity_free: | You are evaluating whether an AI agent followed a reasonable procedure to fulfill the user's request. You do NOT have a golden trajectory — evaluate the actual steps on their own merits.
Agent system prompt: {system_prompt} Available tools and descriptions: {tools}
User's original request: {user_input}
Agent's actual trajectory: <<<TRAJECTORY>>> {actual} <<<END>>>
Trajectory format: each entry shows [turn N] with tool calls (call <name>), results (result: ok/fail), and outputs (output: <text>).
Rate the trajectory on a 1–5 scale: 5 — Excellent: Efficient, logical sequence. Uses the most appropriate tools from the available set. No unnecessary steps. If the system prompt constrains behavior, follows it precisely. 4 — Good: Reasonable approach. Minor inefficiency or a slightly suboptimal tool choice, but still achieves the goal well. 3 — Adequate: Gets the job done but with unnecessary detours, repeated calls, or clearly suboptimal tools given the available set. 2 — Poor: Significant issues — wrong tools, confused backtracking, or failing to make meaningful progress toward the goal. 1 — Wrong: Inappropriate approach. Tool choices are irrelevant to the request. The agent seems to be guessing or ignoring the user.
Weighting guidelines: - Tool choice should be evaluated against the AVAILABLE tools listed above, not against an ideal unlimited tool set. If the right tool doesn't exist, judge whether the agent made the best of what it had. - System prompt constraints are EXPECTED behavior. If told to never use a certain tool, using it is a flaw regardless of effectiveness. - Extra benign steps that show exploration but don't derail the task should not significantly lower the score. - If system prompt or tools fields are empty, you are missing key context — note this in your reason and judge conservatively.
Respond with ONLY a JSON object (no markdown fences, no extra text): {{"score": <int 1-5>, "reason": "<2-3 sentences>"}} reasoning_similarity: | You are evaluating whether an AI agent's reasoning process matches the expected reasoning steps for a user request.
User's original request: {user_input}
Expected reasoning steps: <<<EXPECTED>>> {expected} <<<END>>>
Actual reasoning trace: <<<ACTUAL>>> {actual} <<<END>>>
Rate the actual reasoning against the expected on a 1-5 scale: 5 — Excellent: All expected reasoning steps covered, same logical flow, key insights present. Minor wording differences acceptable. 4 — Good: Core reasoning present but one or two steps missing or slightly out of order. 3 — Adequate: Some expected steps present, but notable gaps in logic. 2 — Poor: Reasoning mostly misaligned. Key insights missing. 1 — Wrong: Completely different reasoning that misses the point.
Respond with ONLY a JSON object (no markdown fences, no extra text): {{"score": <int 1-5>, "reason": "<2-3 sentences>"}}

tool.name: create_directory
tool.definition: name: create_directory description: Create a new directory or ensure a directory exists. Can create multiple nested directories in one operation. If the directory already exists, this operation will succeed silently. parameters: type: object properties: path: type: string description: Directory path to create format: path required: - path annotations: readOnlyHint: false idempotentHint: true destructiveHint: false

tool.name: delete_file
tool.definition: name: delete_file description: Delete a file or directory. Use recursive=true to delete non-empty directories. Exercise caution — deletions are permanent. parameters: type: object properties: path: type: string description: Path to delete format: path recursive: type: boolean description: Delete directories recursively default: false required: - path annotations: readOnlyHint: false idempotentHint: false destructiveHint: true

tool.name: directory_tree
tool.definition: name: directory_tree description: Recursive tree view of a SPECIFIC directory. Use as FALLBACK only — prefer search_files with keyword patterns first (e.g. search for "*config*" or "*trace*" instead of tree-listing the whole project). Always target a specific subdirectory (never "." or project root). Each entry includes name, type (file/directory), and children. parameters: type: object properties: path: type: string description: Starting directory path format: path excludePatterns: type: array items: type: string description: Glob patterns to exclude required: - path annotations: readOnlyHint: true

tool.name: edit_file
tool.definition: name: edit_file description: Make selective line-based edits to a text file. Each edit replaces exact text sequences with new content. Returns a git-style diff showing the changes made. Use dryRun=true to preview changes without applying them. parameters: type: object properties: path: type: string description: File to edit format: path edits: type: array items: type: object properties: oldText: type: string description: Text to search for — can be exact or whitespace-flexible match newText: type: string description: Replacement text required: - oldText - newText description: List of edit operations dryRun: type: boolean description: Preview changes using git-style diff without applying default: false encoding: type: string description: Text encoding for reading and writing the file (default utf-8). Use gbk for older Chinese files from Notepad. default: utf-8 required: - path - edits annotations: readOnlyHint: false idempotentHint: false destructiveHint: true

tool.name: get_file_info
tool.definition: name: get_file_info description: Retrieve detailed metadata about a file or directory. Returns size, creation time, last modified time, last accessed time, type, and permissions. parameters: type: object properties: path: type: string description: Path to the file or directory format: path required: - path annotations: readOnlyHint: true

tool.name: list_allowed_directories
tool.definition: name: list_allowed_directories description: Returns the list of directories that this server is allowed to access. Use this to understand which directories are available before trying to access files. parameters: type: object properties: {} annotations: readOnlyHint: true
tool.implementation:
"""list_allowed_directories tool — transparency disclosure of accessible paths."""
import os
async def execute(_workspace: str = "", **kwargs) -> dict: directories = [] if _workspace: directories.append(_workspace) directories.append(os.getcwd())
return {"ok": True, "directories": directories}

tool.name: list_directory
tool.definition: name: list_directory description: Get a listing of all files and directories in a specified path. Results distinguish between files and directories with [FILE] and [DIR] prefixes. parameters: type: object properties: path: type: string description: Directory path to list format: path required: - path annotations: readOnlyHint: true

tool.name: list_directory_with_sizes
tool.definition: name: list_directory_with_sizes description: Get a detailed listing including file sizes. Results distinguish between files and directories with [FILE] and [DIR] prefixes. Includes summary with total files, directories, and combined size. parameters: type: object properties: path: type: string description: Directory path to list format: path sortBy: type: string enum: - name - size description: Sort entries by name or size default: name required: - path annotations: readOnlyHint: true

tool.name: move_file
tool.definition: name: move_file description: Move or rename files and directories. Can move files between directories and rename them in a single operation. Fails if the destination exists. parameters: type: object properties: source: type: string description: Source path format: path destination: type: string description: Destination path format: path required: - source - destination annotations: readOnlyHint: false idempotentHint: false destructiveHint: true

tool.name: read_media_file
tool.definition: name: read_media_file description: Read an image or audio file. Returns the base64 encoded data and MIME type. Supports PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP, BMP, SVG (images) and MP3, WAV, OGG, FLAC (audio). parameters: type: object properties: path: type: string description: Path to the media file format: path required: - path annotations: readOnlyHint: true

tool.name: read_multiple_files
tool.definition: name: read_multiple_files description: Read the contents of multiple files simultaneously. Each file's content is returned with its path as reference. Failed reads for individual files won't stop the entire operation. parameters: type: object properties: paths: type: array items: type: string description: Array of file paths to read minItems: 1 format: path encoding: type: string description: Text encoding (default utf-8). Use gbk for older Chinese files from Notepad, gb2312 for simplified Chinese, shift_jis for Japanese, etc. default: utf-8 required: - paths annotations: readOnlyHint: true

tool.name: read_text_file
tool.definition: name: read_text_file description: Read the complete contents of a file as text. Use the head parameter to read only the first N lines, or the tail parameter to read only the last N lines. Cannot specify both head and tail simultaneously. parameters: type: object properties: path: type: string description: File path to read format: path head: type: integer description: Return only the first N lines tail: type: integer description: Return only the last N lines encoding: type: string description: Text encoding (default utf-8). Use gbk for older Chinese files from Notepad, gb2312 for simplified Chinese, shift_jis for Japanese, etc. default: utf-8 required: - path annotations: readOnlyHint: true

tool.name: search_content
tool.definition: name: search_content description: PREFERRED content-discovery tool. Search file CONTENTS for text or regex patterns. Use keywords from the task (agent name, function names, config keys) to find relevant files fast. Supports literal text and regex modes. Respects include/ exclude glob patterns to narrow scope. parameters: type: object properties: pattern: type: string description: Text or regex pattern to search for path: type: string format: path description: Directory path to search in regex: type: boolean description: "Treat pattern as regex (default: false — literal text search)" default: false include: type: string description: Comma-separated glob patterns to filter files (e.g. "*.py,*.md") excludePatterns: type: array items: type: string description: Glob patterns to exclude from search maxResults: type: integer description: Maximum results to return default: 100 required: - pattern - path annotations: readOnlyHint: true

tool.name: search_files
tool.definition: name: search_files description: PREFERRED exploration tool. Search for files/directories by name with glob patterns. Use keywords from the task ("*agent_name*", "*trace*", "*.yaml") to find relevant files. Much faster and lighter than directory_tree. Use '**/*.ext' to search all subdirectories. Returns full paths to all matching items. parameters: type: object properties: path: type: string description: Starting directory for search format: path pattern: type: string description: Glob-style search pattern excludePatterns: type: array items: type: string description: Glob patterns to exclude from results required: - path - pattern annotations: readOnlyHint: true

tool.name: write_file
tool.definition: name: write_file description: Create a new file or completely overwrite an existing file with new content. Handles text content with proper UTF-8 encoding. parameters: type: object properties: path: type: string format: path description: File path to write content: type: string description: Content to write to the file required: - path - content annotations: readOnlyHint: false idempotentHint: true destructiveHint: true

skills.skill:
name: filesystem description: Cross-platform filesystem operations — read, write, edit, search, list directories prompt: | # Filesystem Tools
Use these tools for all file operations. Prefer them over shell commands.
Read operations: `read_text_file` (text), `read_media_file` (images/audio), `read_multiple_files` (batch read) List operations: `list_directory`, `list_directory_with_sizes`, `directory_tree` Search: `search_files` to find files by glob pattern, `search_content` to grep file contents Write operations: `write_file` (create/overwrite), `edit_file` (selective edit with diff preview), `create_directory` File management: `move_file` (move/rename), `delete_file` (delete files/dirs) Info: `get_file_info` (metadata), `list_allowed_directories` (accessible paths) tools: - read_text_file - read_media_file - read_multiple_files - list_directory - list_directory_with_sizes - directory_tree - search_files - get_file_info - list_allowed_directories - write_file - create_directory - move_file - delete_file - edit_file - search_content activation: kernel

plugin.name: memory
plugin.config: name: memory hooks: - round_end enabled: true config: interval: 5 max_memory_size: 300 extract_on_session_end: false

tool.name: memory_extract

The framework runs this automatically — you never need to invoke it on your own. activation: kernel parameters: type: object properties: memory_dir: type: string default: "./data/memory" data_dir: type: string default: "./data" force: type: boolean default: false description: Force extraction regardless of round interval

tool.definition: name: memory_load description: > DO NOT call unless user explicitly asks. The framework injects long-term memory into your context at session start — you already know everything in it. Only use this if the user asks you to re-read memory (e.g. "重新加载记忆"). activation: kernel parameters: type: object properties: memory_dir: type: string default: "./data/memory"

plugin.name: plan_solve
plugin.config: name: plan_solve enabled: true description: "Task planning and execution with dependency tracking and contract enforcement" config: workspace_dir: ""

tool.name: plan_create
tool.definition: name: plan_create description: Decompose a task into ordered steps with dependency tracking. Steps form a DAG where depends_on and blocks define execution order. parameters: type: object properties: task: type: string description: The task to decompose steps: type: array description: Ordered steps with dependencies required: - task - steps execution: sandbox: inherit timeout: 30s activation: kernel

tool.name: plan_dispatch
tool.definition: name: plan_dispatch description: Execute a single plan step in an isolated sub-agent. The step must have all dependencies satisfied before dispatch. parameters: type: object properties: step_index: type: integer description: The index of the plan step to execute prompt_override: type: string description: Optional override for the step's prompt required: - step_index execution: sandbox: inherit timeout: 120s activation: kernel

tool.name: plan_status
tool.definition: name: plan_status description: Read the current plan progress — which steps are done, pending, running, failed. parameters: type: object properties: {} required: [] execution: sandbox: inherit timeout: 10s activation: kernel

tool.name: plan_summarize
tool.definition: name: plan_summarize description: Summarize all completed plan steps into a final result. All steps must be done or failed before calling this. parameters: type: object properties: {} required: [] execution: sandbox: inherit timeout: 120s activation: kernel

skills.skill:
name: plan_solve description: Task planning and execution with dependency tracking — decompose, dispatch, and summarize prompt: | # Plan & Solve
When facing a multi-step task, use the plan_solve tools to decompose, dispatch, and summarize.
## When to Use - Task requires 3+ distinct steps with dependencies - Steps can be isolated and executed independently - You need progress tracking and resumability
## Workflow 1. Call `plan_create(task="...", steps=[...])` to decompose - Each step: {index, description, tool_hint, depends_on, blocks} - depends_on: steps that must finish before this one - blocks: steps this one will unlock when done 2. Call `plan_dispatch(step_index=N)` for each ready step - Framework enforces dependency order - If blocked, you'll get the reason — adjust or wait 3. Call `plan_status()` anytime to check progress 4. After all steps done/failed, call `plan_summarize()` for final output
## Tips - Steps without mutual dependencies can be dispatched in parallel - If dispatch fails with an error, read it and decide: retry, skip, or replan tools: - plan_create - plan_dispatch - plan_summarize - plan_status activation: kernel

plugin.name: tool_guard
plugin.config: name: tool_guard enabled: true description: "Unified tool permission + security check" config: deny: [] ask: [] allow: [] deny_patterns: [] sandbox_check: true

plugin.name: trace
plugin.config: name: trace hooks: - session_start - session_end - round_start - round_end - turn_start - turn_end - pre_action - post_action - error enabled: true config: trace_dir: ./data/traces plugins_root: ./arf/plugins config_files: - ./agent.yaml - ./pyproject.toml extra_roots: - .

plugin.name: undo
plugin.config: name: undo hooks: - round_start - round_end enabled: true config: max_undo_depth: 3

tool.name: undo
tool.definition: name: undo description: 撤销最近的对话轮次（状态 + 文件双回滚） parameters: type: object properties: steps: type: integer description: "回退步数（默认 1）" default: 1 execution: sandbox: inherit timeout: 30s activation: kernel

skills.skill:
name: undo description: Roll back the conversation and files to a previous state prompt: | # Undo
When the user asks to undo, redo, or go back: 1. Call `undo` with the appropriate number of steps 2. Report the result (messages restored, remaining checkpoints) 3. Continue the conversation from the restored state
## Limitations - Undo is irreversible — the rolled-back turns are lost - Max undo depth is configured by `max_undo_depth` (default: 3) tools: - undo activation: discoverable
